_meta.source: game.html buildEpisodes() v3.2 + Muse QA fixes (2026-11-12)
_meta.note: ${PETS.*} placeholders are preserved literally; interpolate at load time from the 5-pet squad config (URL params -> localStorage -> defaults Poppy/Mochi/Luna/Boba/Buster). Do not hand-edit episode content here; game.html is the source of truth.

ostentatious.def_en: Excessively showy and designed to flex or attract attention.
ostentatious.def_zh: 炫耀卖弄的；浮夸招摇的
ostentatious.root: ostent (stretch out to view) → shoving your price tag in everyone's face.
ostentatious.story_hook: Wearing a 3-foot solid gold sailboat on top of your wig just to eat cereal.
ostentatious.savage_roast: Loud flexing with zero taste. Bringing a diamond-crusted Stanley cup to 1st-period math.

obsequious.def_en: Obedient or attentive to an excessive degree; sucking up to power.
obsequious.def_zh: 谄媚的；卑躬屈膝溜须拍马的
obsequious.root: ob- (toward) + sequi (follow) → following VIPs around like a desperate servant.
obsequious.story_hook: ${PETS.c2} massaging the automatic feeder with both paws hoping extra salmon drops out.
obsequious.savage_roast: Hall-of-Fame glazing. Laughing way too hard at the teacher's unfunny joke for extra credit.

aloof.def_zh: 高冷疏离的；置身事外的
aloof.root: steering a ship windward away from the crowd → staying 10 feet away from drama.
aloof.story_hook: ${PETS.c1} sitting on the highest bookshelf watching humans panic without blinking.
aloof.savage_roast: Acting too cool to reply in the group chat while screenshotting everything in 0.2s.

sycophant.def_en: A person who sucks up to important people to gain an advantage.
sycophant.root: Greek sykophantes → a professional yes-man trading dignity for perks.
sycophant.story_hook: Clapping and crying tears of joy because the King tied his own shoelaces.
sycophant.savage_roast: The group project partner who writes zero slides but emails the teacher praising her rubric.

supercilious.def_en: Behaving as though one is superior to everyone else.
supercilious.def_zh: 目中无人的；高傲挑眉看人的
supercilious.root: super- (above) + cilium (eyebrow) → raising one eyebrow like everyone else is a peasant.
supercilious.story_hook: A royal poodle tilting its nose 45 degrees into the air to ignore stray cats.
supercilious.savage_roast: Main-character arrogance. Looking at everyone in the hallway like low-budget NPCs.

candid.def_en: Truthful, blunt, and straightforward; zero filter.
candid.def_zh: 直言不讳的；坦率真诚的
candid.root: candidus (bright white/pure) → unvarnished truth with zero sugarcoating.
candid.story_hook: ${PETS.c2} telling the King straight up that his royal robe looks like a giant bath towel.
candid.savage_roast: Telling your bestie their new haircut looks like a chewed broom before they post it on IG.

chat.en: Besties, bad news: France is broke. Stop buying ostentatious diamond wigs just to flex at Tuesday tea!
chat.zh: 家人们坏消息：法兰西国库破产了！别为了周二下午茶显摆，再买那些【浮夸炫耀的】钻石假发了！

chat.en: Relax! Once the King reads my obsequious poem praising his royal jawline, he'll double my allowance.
chat.zh: 淡定！等国王读完我那首【卑躬屈膝溜须拍马】狂吹他下颌线的赞美诗，立马给我零花钱翻倍。

chat.en: Fascinating. I usually stay aloof from human nonsense, yet watching nobles bankrupt a country for compliments is cinema.
chat.zh: 真精彩。我向来对人类的蠢事保持【高冷疏离】，但围观贵族为了听彩虹屁把国家搞破产，属实是年度大戏。

chat.en: Translation: The Duke is a full-time sycophant trading dignity for cake! Also, ${PETS.c3} and I just ate the King's salmon.
chat.zh: 翻译成人话：公爵就是个拿尊严换蛋糕的全职【马屁精】！顺便说一句，我和 ${PETS.c3} 刚偷吃了国王的三文鱼。

chat.en: How dare stray pets roast me! My royal bloodline entitles me to give you a supercilious sneer!
chat.zh: 区区小猫小狗敢怼我！凭我高贵的血统，完全有资格赏你们一个【目中无人的】高傲冷笑！

chat.en: WOOF! Did ${PETS.c4} screenshot that?! The Duke is acting super arrogant while ${PETS.c1} is about to drop some candid truth bombs!
chat.zh: 汪！${PETS.c4} 截图了吗？！公爵还在那高傲装大爷，${PETS.c1} 马上就要对他来一番【直言不讳的】大实话暴击了！

boss.headline: Duke Orléans Tried to Frame ${PETS.c2} & ${PETS.d1}!
boss.headline_zh: 奥尔良公爵想把偷吃蛋糕的锅甩给 ${PETS.c2} 和 ${PETS.d1}！
boss.context: The Duke knocked over the Queen's cake, wiped the frosting off his chin, and put on a fake innocent face to blame ${PETS.c2}. Expose his fake innocence:
boss.context_zh: 公爵打翻了王后的多层奶油蛋糕，擦掉下巴上的奶油，装出一副无辜纯洁的表情甩锅给 ${PETS.c2}。快选出精准揭穿他“假装无辜”的 SAT 词：
boss.sentence: "Drop the innocent act, Duke! Your apology is totally ______ — ${PETS.c3} caught you on 4K licking the frosting!"
boss.sentence_zh: “收起你那套无辜演技吧公爵！你的道歉完全是【虚伪装纯的】——${PETS.c3} 都拍下你偷舔奶油的 4K 证据了！”

options.zh: 虚伪狡诈的；假装无辜/不知情的
options.desc: Insincere; pretending to be more innocent than one really is

options.zh: 真正天真无邪的；坦率真诚的
options.desc: Truly innocent, artless, and candid; childlike honesty

boss.wasted_title: 💀 VERBALLY WASTED // You Called the Scheming Duke a Pure Angel!
boss.wasted_body: Ingenuous means genuinely innocent! The Duke cried happy tears and forced ${PETS.c2} and ${PETS.d1} to brush his 30-pound powdered wig!
boss.wasted_zh: 【社死翻车】Ingenuous 是“真纯洁无瑕”！公爵听完感动得罚 ${PETS.c2} 和 ${PETS.d1} 每天给他梳 30 斤重的假发！记住：IN-genuous = 真纯真；DIS-ingenuous = 装纯真/虚伪！
boss.win_body: BOOM! Disingenuous (fake-innocent / insincere) exposed his act in front of the whole palace!
boss.win_zh: 漂亮绝杀！Disingenuous（虚伪装无辜）当场戳破公爵的绿茶演技，全场贵族笑翻！

sat.passage: In the final decade before the French Revolution, memoirs from Versailles reveal a court culture built on ______ allegiance: courtiers who lavished the monarchy with extravagant flattery in public were frequently the very first to betray royal confidences to rival factions the moment financial subsidies dried up.
sat.passage_zh: 【中文微距精译】在法国大革命爆发前的最后十年里，凡尔赛宫回忆录揭示了一种建立在（______）效忠之上的宫廷文化：那些在公开场合对王室极尽【浮夸奉承】的朝臣，一旦财政津贴断绝，往往第一个向敌对派系【背叛出卖王室机密】。

choices.zh: 背信弃义的；当面一套背后一套的

sat.hack_en: Look at the colon (:)—everything after it defines the blank! Flattering in public while 'betraying royal confidences' behind their back is the exact definition of perfidious (deceitful and untrustworthy).
sat.hack_zh: 【10秒秒题口诀】盯紧冒号（:）后面的同义解释！当面狂拍马屁（extravagant flattery），背后立刻出卖机密（betray royal confidences），这种两面三刀的背叛对应的唯一高阶词就是 perfidious（背信弃义的）！

empirical.def_en: Based on real observation and experiments rather than pure theory.
empirical.def_zh: 实证的；基于观察与实验证据的
empirical.root: empeirikos (experienced) → hard receipts you can test with your own eyes.
empirical.story_hook: ${PETS.c2} knocking 10 cups off the table one by one to test gravity with a stopwatch.
empirical.savage_roast: Bringing timestamped screenshot receipts instead of 'trust me bro'.

corroborate.def_en: To confirm or back up a claim with new independent evidence.
corroborate.root: cor- + robur (oak strength) → making a story solid as oak with backup proof.
corroborate.story_hook: Two separate pet cameras both catching ${PETS.c2} and ${PETS.d1} opening the fridge at 2 AM.
corroborate.savage_roast: When ${PETS.c3} backs up your story in the group chat with a second video angle.

refute.def_en: To prove a statement or theory to be completely wrong; disprove.
refute.def_zh: 驳倒；用证据证明…是错的
refute.root: re- (back) + futare (beat) → beating down a fake claim with facts.
refute.story_hook: ${PETS.c1} using a thermal camera to prove ${PETS.d1} WAS sleeping on the couch.
refute.savage_roast: Destroying someone's fake excuse with one screenshot.

equivocate.def_en: To use vague, double-meaning language to dodge the truth.
equivocate.def_zh: 模棱两可地说；支吾搪塞
equivocate.root: equi- (equal) + voc (voice) → talking both sides so nobody can pin you down.
equivocate.story_hook: Asked 'Did you eat the fish?', ${PETS.c2} says 'Define the concept of eating.'
equivocate.savage_roast: Politician-level dodging when Mom asks what you got on the Chemistry test.

spurious.def_en: False or fake; not being what it claims to be.
spurious.root: Latin spurius (counterfeit) → fake facts dressed up as science.
spurious.story_hook: A '100% Real Tuna' treat that turns out to be cardboard.
spurious.savage_roast: Fake TikTok 'science' claiming sleeping on your textbook transfers knowledge by osmosis.

bolster.def_en: To support, strengthen, or prop up an argument.
bolster.def_zh: 巩固；强化支持（论点或信心）
bolster.root: bolster (a thick structural cushion) → propping up a claim so it stands strong.
bolster.story_hook: Stacking three extra pillows under ${PETS.c4}'s chin during nap time.
bolster.savage_roast: Adding three Harvard citations to your essay 5 minutes before the deadline.

chat.en: Guys, look through the telescope! I have empirical proof that moons orbit Jupiter!
chat.zh: 伙计们快看望远镜！我有【实证观测】数据证明卫星在绕着木星转！

chat.en: Put that tube away! Your spurious star drawings are just smudges on the glass!
chat.zh: 把那根管子收起来！你那些【虚假伪造的】星图不过是镜片上的油污罢了！

chat.en: Actually, Kepler's independent orbital math helped corroborate Galileo's logs.
chat.zh: 事实上，开普勒独立计算的行星轨道数据已经【证实并印证】了伽利略的观测记录。

chat.en: Wait—the Inquisitor can't refute the telescope math, so his strategy is closing his eyes?! ${PETS.c4}, clip that!
chat.zh: 等等——审判官没法用证据【驳倒】望远镜数据，所以他的战术是直接闭眼不看？！${PETS.c4} 快截下来！

chat.en: I hate drama, so I will equivocate and say Earth moves 'poetically' while staying still 'legally'.
chat.zh: 我不想惹事，所以我决定【模棱两可和稀泥】：地球在诗歌层面在转，但在法律层面不动。

chat.en: WOOF! Every clear night brings new telescope photos to bolster Team Galileo! Science wins!
chat.zh: 汪！每个晴朗夜晚的新望远镜照片都在进一步【巩固支持】伽利略战队！科学必胜！

boss.headline: The Inquisitor Drops a Fake 'Logic Trap'!
boss.headline_zh: 审判官抛出了一个看似有理的“伪逻辑陷阱”！
boss.context: He argues: 'If Earth spun at 1,000 mph, birds would fly backward into space!' It sounds clever for two seconds, but the physics is totally wrong. Call out his fake-smart claim:
boss.context_zh: 他声称：“如果地球以每小时1000英里自转，鸟儿一飞起来就会被甩进外太空！”听起来像那么回事，但物理学上完全是错的。选出揭穿“似是而非”的词：
boss.sentence: "Nice try, but that bird argument is completely ______ — even ${PETS.d1} knows the air spins WITH the Earth!"
boss.sentence_zh: “想得美，但你那个小鸟论证完全是【似是而非、表面有理实则错误的】——连 ${PETS.d1} 都知道大气层是跟着地球一起转的！”

options.zh: 似是而非的；表面有理实则错误的
options.desc: Sounding smart on the surface, but actually false
Having keen mental wisdom and brilliant judgment

boss.wasted_title: 💀 VERBALLY WASTED // You Praised Flat-Earth Physics as Genius!
boss.wasted_body: Sagacious means deeply wise! The Inquisitor made ${PETS.c2} President of the Flat-Cheese Moon Club!
boss.wasted_zh: 【社死翻车】Sagacious 是“极其睿智的”！你把他的歪理夸成了绝世智慧！记住：SPEC-ious = 表面看起来像（Spec），实则是假货！
boss.win_body: SAVAGE! Specious is the #1 SAT word for something that sounds convincing at first glance but is logically flawed!
boss.win_zh: 精准暴击！Specious（似是而非的）是机考 SAT 逻辑题最爱考的高频核心词！

sat.passage: Although seventeenth-century critics attempted to ______ Galileo's telescopic findings by claiming that curved glass lenses created optical illusions, subsequent advancements in lens precision eliminated those distortions and vindicated his original measurements.
sat.passage_zh: 【中文微距精译】尽管17世纪的批评家试图通过声称弯曲的玻璃镜片会产生视觉错觉来（______）伽利略的望远镜发现，但随后镜片打磨精度的进步【消除了这些失真】并【证实了他最初测量数据的正确性】。
sat.hack_en: Spot the 'Although' contrast! Critics accused his lenses of creating 'illusions' to weaken his findings—which is the exact definition of undermine.
sat.hack_zh: 【10秒秒题口诀】抓住句首 Although 的转折逻辑！后半句说新镜片证实（vindicated）了他的数据，说明前半句批评家说镜片有错觉是为了【削弱、动摇】他的发现，秒选 undermine！

dormant.root: dormire (to sleep, like dorm room) → sleeping until it wakes up angry.
dormant.story_hook: ${PETS.c2} sleeping like a furry loaf for 14 hours until a snack bag rustles.
dormant.savage_roast: Your study motivation staying completely asleep until 11:55 PM on Sunday.

anomaly.def_en: Something weird that deviates from what is normal or expected.
anomaly.root: an- (not) + homalos (regular) → a glitch in the normal pattern.
anomaly.story_hook: It raining roast chicken instead of water on a Tuesday afternoon.
anomaly.savage_roast: When the kid who sleeps in class randomly gets 100% on the AP Chem curve.

volatile.def_en: Unstable and likely to explode or change rapidly for the worse.
volatile.root: volare (to fly) → ready to blow its lid at any second.
volatile.story_hook: A shaken bottle of fizzy soda waiting for someone to twist the cap.
volatile.savage_roast: The group chat 3 seconds after someone brings up grades or crushes.

exacerbate.def_en: To make a bad situation even worse.
exacerbate.root: ex- + acerbus (harsh) → pouring hot sauce on a papercut.
exacerbate.story_hook: Trying to wipe muddy pawprints off a white rug using a chocolate towel.
exacerbate.savage_roast: Texting 'Calm down lol' to someone who is already mad.

ameliorate.def_en: To make a bad or painful situation better and more bearable.
ameliorate.root: melior (better) → upgrading a disaster into something survivable.
ameliorate.story_hook: Giving a grumpy cat a heated blanket and salmon after a vet visit.
ameliorate.savage_roast: The teacher adding a 15-point curve so the whole class doesn't fail.

catalyst.def_en: An event or person that sparks a massive, rapid change.
catalyst.def_zh: 催化剂；引发巨变的导火索
catalyst.root: kata- + lyein (loosen) → the single spark that starts a chain reaction.
catalyst.story_hook: One red laser dot triggering a 5-pet stampede with ${PETS.c3}, ${PETS.c4}, and ${PETS.d1}.
catalyst.savage_roast: One leaked screenshot causing three friend groups to reorganize before lunch.

chat.en: Neighbors, chill! Mount Vesuvius has been dormant for centuries. That smoke is just a BBQ!
chat.zh: 邻居们淡定！维苏威火山已经【休眠】好几百年了，那团黑烟只是有人在烤肉，别影响房价！

chat.en: Bro, a 12-mile pillar of fire shooting into the sky is a massive geological anomaly!
chat.zh: 老兄，直冲12英里高空的火柱绝不正常，这是极其罕见的地质【反常现象】！

chat.en: My sensors show the magma chamber is super volatile. Staying for the pool party has a 0% survival rate.
chat.zh: 我的传感器显示岩浆房极其【不稳定且易爆发】。留下来开泳池派对的生还率为零。

chat.en: Stop panicking! Your texts will exacerbate chariot traffic on the highway!
chat.zh: 别制造恐慌！你们这些消息只会让主干道上的马车堵车更加【恶化】！

chat.en: You think a $5 coupon for the Roman baths will ameliorate a rain of boiling lava rocks ruining my fur?!
chat.zh: 你觉得发一张五块钱的澡堂优惠券就能【改善缓解】天上下沸腾火山石烫坏我毛发的绝境吗？！

chat.en: WOOF! That earthquake was the final catalyst—grab ${PETS.c2} and ${PETS.c3} and run to the boats NOW!
chat.zh: 汪！刚才那次地震成了最后的【催化剂导火索】——快抱上 ${PETS.c2} 和 ${PETS.c3} 往船上跑！

boss.headline: Marcus Thinks the Eruption Will Pass in 5 Minutes!
boss.headline_zh: 物业主任 Marcus 居然觉得火山喷发五分钟就会停！
boss.context: Pumice stones are raining down, yet Marcus insists this volcano eruption is just a 'short, temporary summer shower'. Roast his delusion:
boss.context_zh: 火山石都在往下砸了，Marcus 还嘴硬说这场火山爆发只是“转瞬即逝的五分钟阵雨”。选出精准表达“短暂、转瞬即逝”的 SAT 词怼醒他：
boss.sentence: "Marcus, 20 feet of volcanic ash is NOT some ______ drizzle—it's permanent!"
boss.sentence_zh: “Marcus，二十英尺厚的火山灰可不是什么【转瞬即逝的】小阵雨——它是永久性的！”

options.zh: 转瞬即逝的；极其短暂的
options.desc: Lasting for a very short time; fleeting
Never ending or changing; lasting forever

boss.wasted_title: 💀 VERBALLY WASTED // Your Sentence Made Zero Sense!
boss.wasted_body: Perpetual means forever! Saying 'It's NOT perpetual, it's permanent' contradicted itself!
boss.wasted_zh: 【社死翻车】Perpetual 是“永久的”！说“这不是永久的，这是永久的”逻辑自相矛盾！记住：Ephemeral = 像蜉蝣或限时动态一样转瞬即逝！
boss.win_body: BOOM! Ephemeral (fleeting / short-lived) woke Marcus up and he finally sprinted to the harbor!
boss.win_zh: 满分暴击！Ephemeral（转瞬即逝的）是机考 SAT 必考词，Marcus 终于拎起长袍逃命去了！

sat.passage: Far from causing a merely localized disruption, the 1815 eruption of Mount Tambora triggered ______ climatic shifts across the Northern Hemisphere: sulfate aerosols reflected enough solar radiation to plunge summer temperatures below freezing and devastate harvests on three continents.
sat.passage_zh: 【中文微距精译】1815年坦博拉火山的爆发远非仅造成局部干扰，而是在整个北半球引发了（______）气候巨变：硫酸盐气溶胶反射了大量太阳辐射，足以【使夏季气温骤降至冰点以下】并【摧毁三大洲的农作物收成】。
sat.hack_en: Look at the extreme scale after the colon: 'freezing summers' and 'devastated harvests on three continents.' Only cataclysmic (large-scale violent disaster) matches!
sat.hack_zh: 【10秒秒题口诀】看冒号后的极端结果：夏天结冰、三大洲庄稼绝收！只有 cataclysmic（毁灭性的、大灾难级的）能匹配这种全球级别的破坏力！
